positions.name: SettledAdoptionDecision
positions.frame: Is the adoption and its timeline performed here as a ratified, settled course of action rather than a proposal still being argued?
positions.why: src-1 declares adoption with 'we are adopting' — performed-act ratification language, not a proposal on offer. src-3 commits to a timeline ('starts next quarter') as settled schedule rather than tentative plan. src-4 and src-6 restate both in the compressed bolded label form, carrying the same ratifying, authority-ranking register (footed to Quinton as principal) rather than re-arguing them. The conviction reads across all four land in 'decision,' distinguishing them from the performance figure, which stays in 'claim' register even when restated — held in tension here only insofar as the set groups exclusively the ratified moves and leaves the evidential claim outside it.

positions.name: PerformanceClaimAsEvidence
positions.frame: Is the 15x performance figure presented as an evidential claim still open to challenge, rather than a ratified fact like the adoption decision?
positions.why: src-2 asserts the comparative performance figure as an unhedged but evidentiary claim ('It handles columnar queries 15x faster') — rational-persuasion/expert framing, market-pricing proportionality, and a 'claim' conviction read rather than 'decision.' src-5 restates the same figure in the bolded summary form but keeps the same evidential character rather than shifting into ratification language, so the two cohere under a distinct frame from the adoption/timeline decision group even though both originate from the same speaker in the same document.
